Top One Futures Account Comparison: Elite vs. Instant vs. Ignite accounts
Top One Futures Account Comparison: Elite vs. Instant vs. Ignite accounts

A side-by-side comparison of the Elite, Instant Sim Funded, and Ignite account models to help you choose the right path to funding.

Updated over a month ago

Finding the right path to funding depends on your trading style, risk tolerance, and how quickly you want to access a funded environment. Below is a detailed breakdown of the three account models offered by Top One Futures: Elite, Instant Sim Funded, and Ignite.

 

1-Step Elite Evaluation

The 1-Step Elite Evaluation is designed as a traditional evaluation pathway for disciplined traders. Under this model, you must successfully reach a specific profit target while adhering to risk management rules to prove your trading skills. Once the profit target is reached and the Elite Evaluation is passed, an activation fee is required to transition from the Evaluation phase to a funded environment where you then can work towards a payout.

 

This path is ideal for traders who are confident in their ability to pass evaluations and want to benefit from a 25% consistency rule, which is more generous than the rules found in the Instant or Ignite account models.

Contract Rollovers – Futures Contracts Explained

What contract rollovers are, how to read a futures contract code, why low-volume contracts are risky, and how to check which contract is active.

October 2, 2026

In this article we explain what contract rollovers are, why they matter for traders, how to read a futures contract code, and how to check which contract is currently the active one so you can roll over at the right time.

 

What is a futures contract?

A futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a specific future date. Unlike stocks, futures contracts have an expiration date. For example, equity index futures like the S&P 500 or the NASDAQ-100 are listed with multiple expiration months throughout the year (March, June, September, December, etc.). Each expiration month represents a separate contract.

 

Understanding futures contract codes

Every CME futures contract has a specific symbol structure: [Product Symbol] + [Month Code] + [Year].

 

1. Product symbol

This identifies the underlying asset.

2. Month code (letter)

Futures contracts use a standardized letter to represent the expiration month. These month codes are globally standardized across futures markets.

While the standard month codes (like U, V, X) are globally standardized across futures markets, not every instrument follows the same rollover schedule. Depending on what you are trading, you will need to watch for different expiration cycles.

Rollover frequency

This means it is the September 2026 E-mini S&P 500 futures contract.

 

Why should we roll over? The real risk: low volume contracts

As a futures contract approaches expiration, trading activity gradually shifts to the next contract month listed on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. This means the expiring contract begins to lose trading volume, open interest, and order book depth.

 

Front month vs. back months

Contract

	

What it is




Front month

	

The contract with the closest expiration date that still has the highest trading volume and open interest. It is the most "active" contract where most trading occurs. This is the one to trade




Back months

	

Contracts that expire further in the future. While they exist in the order book, they typically have very low volume and thin liquidity. Avoid these

Why it matters: traders should almost always trade the front month. Trading a back month by mistake can lead to serious risks.

 

Risks of trading low-volume contracts

Risk factor

	

Impact on trading




Wider spreads

	

Very large bid-ask spreads, immediately putting you in big drawdown when entering




Slippage risk

	

Market orders fill at worse prices, poor stop-loss execution with huge slippage risk




Thin order books

	

Small trades cause sharp price jumps, unstable behavior, technical levels do not react cleanly




Unreliable price action

	

Irregular price movements and gaps not present in the active contract

Important, responsibility of the trader: Top One Futures is not responsible for losses exceeding normal risk parameters caused by trading low-volume or close-to-expired contracts. It is the trader's sole responsibility to ensure they are trading the correct, active contract. Trading "thin" or close-to-expired contracts leads to severe slippage (market orders and stop losses may fill at much worse prices) and extreme volatility (small trades can cause massive, erratic price jumps).

How to check which contract we are trading

To make sure you are trading the correct futures contract, always confirm where the liquidity currently is, or use a rollover calendar.

 

Check volume on the CME website

The most reliable source is the Chicago Mercantile Exchange website. On the product page (for example, Gold futures), you can:

Compare trading volume across all listed contract months

Check open interest

Confirm expiration dates

Identify which contract is the current front month

The contract with the highest volume is typically the active contract. For example, you can find the Micro Gold volume page here: CME Micro Gold volume.

 

Important: the examples below are provided for educational purposes only and should not be relied upon as confirmation of the current active contract. Always verify which contract is currently active before trading.

 

This article was written on February 25, 2026. On that date, the active contract for Micro Gold (MGC) is the April 2026 contract. As you can see, APR 2026 has the highest volume by far and traders should trade on this contract. April = J, 2026 = 6, so the right contract is MGCJ6.
​

How is it calculated?

The Daily Loss Limit is a dynamic value calculated from your previous day's closing balance. To find your breach level for the current day, subtract the allowed daily loss from that balance.

$26,000 - $625 = $25,375

If your account's equity drops to $25,375 at any point during the current trading day, the system will automatically execute market orders to liquidate all of your open positions.

Important disclaimer: the Daily Drawdown Limit (DLL) is a risk management tool, not a stop loss. It should never be relied on to close your trades at a specific loss amount. Due to market volatility, slippage, and execution speed, the DLL can execute late, early, at a different price than you expect, or fail to trigger. If you want to control your risk as best as possible, you must place hard stop loss orders directly on your trades. Relying solely on the DLL can result in losing more than intended. Top One Futures is not responsible for any losses that exceed the daily drawdown limit. Any loss beyond your allowed threshold is the trader's responsibility.

Our copy trading policy: same type and same size only, what counts as prohibited copy trading, correlated assets, and your responsibility when using a trade copier.

Updated over a week ago

Top One Futures allows you to copy trades to manage multiple accounts efficiently. However, to maintain risk integrity, copy trading is strictly limited to accounts of the exact same type and exact same size. Mixing different account programs, sizes, or trying to bypass these rules through manual mirroring or correlated assets is a strict violation of our terms.

 

1. The core rule: same type, same size

You can only copy trades between accounts that belong to the identical program and share the same size.

Example

	

Allowed?




Elite ACCESS $50K to another Elite ACCESS $50K

	

Allowed




Ignite Instant Funding $100K to another Ignite Instant Funding $100K

	

Allowed




Elite ACCESS with Elite Daily

	

Prohibited (different type)




Instant Sim Funded with Ignite

	

Prohibited (different type)




Instant Sim Funded $50K with Instant Sim Funded $100K

	

Prohibited (different size)

The prohibited examples above are not an exhaustive list.

 

2. What counts as prohibited copy trading?

Copy trading violations are not just limited to software settings. The following actions are classified as unauthorized copy trading:

Violation

	

What it means




A. Copying different accounts or sizes together

	

Using a trade copier to link, bridge, or trade different account types or different account sizes together at the same time




B. Manual mirroring (delayed entries)

	

Manually entering the same trade across different account types or sizes to copy your own positions. If you buy or sell the same instrument across mismatched accounts, even if it is minutes or an hour later, it is still classified as copy trading. As long as the position is still active on your first account and the different account size or type goes in the same direction as well, it is classified as copy trading




C. Correlated asset trading

	

Trading the same direction on highly correlated assets across different account types or sizes. Highly correlated instruments move closely together, meaning trading them in the same direction simultaneously is a strict violation

Correlated assets: what is and is not allowed

Category

	

Examples




Considered correlated (prohibited), including but not limited to

	

ES (S&P 500) and NQ (Nasdaq), or YM (Dow Jones) and RTY (Russell 2000) in the same direction across mismatched accounts. Mini and micro versions: ES and MES, or NQ and MNQ in the same direction across mismatched accounts




Not considered correlated (allowed)

	

Trading completely unrelated asset classes at the same time across different account types. For example, going long on NQ (Nasdaq) in your Instant Sim Funded account while simultaneously going long on CL (Crude Oil) or GC (Gold) in your Elite Daily account is acceptable

Examples of a violation:

You have an Instant Sim Funded account and an Elite Daily account. Opening a long position on ES in one account, and then opening a long position on NQ in the other account while the first position is still active, is a violation.

You have an Ignite Instant Funding account and an Elite ACCESS account. Opening a long position on GC in one account, and then opening a long position on SI in the other account while the first position is still active, is a violation.

 

3. Consequences of a violation

Violating this Copy Trading Policy is treated as a prohibited trading practice. If we find a violation:

Profits made through the violation may be removed, and any related payout request could be denied.

In serious or repeated cases, the accounts involved may be terminated.

For more details, see our Prohibited Trading Practices article.

 

Does Top One Futures provide its own trade copier software?

Yes! We provide a trade copier feature built directly into our trading platform, Tradovate. You can set up and manage your trade copier configurations right from within the platform. For more information about Group Trading, refer to this FAQ article from Tradovate.

 

What does "individual trading responsibility" mean for copy trading?

It means that each trader must operate independently. Even if you are using our trade copier for your own accounts, certain actions are strictly not allowed because they violate the spirit of individual trading:

Executing the same trades as another person or account.

Coordinated trading with relatives or friends.

Following signal services, Telegram groups, Discord calls, or any shared trade alert system.

Subscribing to any service that results in mirrored trades across different accounts.

We expect unique strategies per trader, not correlated or synchronized actions between different individuals or entities.

 

Note on copy trading between firms

Top One Futures allows copy trading between your own accounts at different firms, including through third-party platforms. Your master account may be held at Top One Futures or another firm, provided all accounts involved are owned by you and all trades reflect your own strategy and discretion.
​

Copying trades from accounts owned by anyone else is strictly prohibited. Signal following, group trading, or mirroring someone else’s trades is also strictly prohibited.

 

Your responsibility for copy trading adjustments and outcomes

Each trader is solely responsible for the configuration, supervision, and final outcomes of all trades executed via third-party copy trading software.

Scope of responsibility

	

Detail




Execution errors

	

Top One Futures is not responsible for trades that fail to copy, copy incorrectly, or execute at unintended times or sizes




Account outcomes

	

Any account loss or breach, including but not limited to Maximum Drawdown violations or Daily Loss Limit hits resulting from third-party software activity, is the sole responsibility of the trader




No reversals

	

We cannot void losses, reset accounts, or provide refunds for trades originated by external software, regardless of whether the trader manually initiated the trade or not

October 16, 2026

All traders must place at least one trade every 14 calendar days to keep their account in good standing. This article explains how the Inactivity Rule works, what happens if you break it, and how to avoid it.

 

What is the Inactivity Rule?

Rule detail

	

How it works




Requirement

	

At least one trade (entry and exit) must occur within a 14-day window, starting from your most recent trade




Counting days

	

The 14-day window includes weekends and holidays, not just business days




Exact Calculation

	

The 14-day rule is calculated strictly down to the exact hour and minute (336 consecutive hours) from the timestamp of your most recent trade.
It is not based on calendar day cutoffs (e.g., midnight).

Example: If your last trade was on the April 1st at 13:00 UTC, your 14-day window expires on April 15th at 13:00 UTC sharp.

What happens if I don't trade for 14 days?

If no trades are placed within any 14-day period:

Your account will be marked inactive.

The account will receive a hard breach and be closed permanently.

All progress and profits on the account will be lost.

Example: if your last trade was on April 1st, you must place your next trade no later than April 15th to avoid being breached for inactivity.

 

Tips to avoid inactivity

Set a reminder on your phone or calendar every 10 to 12 days.

Even one small trade (meeting our 10-second minimum) is enough to stay active.

Do not wait until the last minute, give yourself a buffer.

Please note: an inactivity breach is permanent. Keep your account active with at least one trade every 14 calendar days.

Frequently asked questions

How many payouts do I need before I can go live?
For most accounts, you need 3 successful payouts. Elite Daily accounts are the exception and require 5 successful payouts. In some cases a trader may be transitioned to a Live Account sooner, but the numbers above are the standard requirement.

 

If I get selected to move to live, can I choose to stay in Sim Funding?
No. If you are selected to move to live, your options are to begin trading live or to close your Sim Funded account. You may not voluntarily close your live account and move back to Sim. Sim trading should be seen as a gateway to trading live, having your consistency rule removed, receiving unlimited payouts, and scaling your capital. Any attempts to intentionally breach accounts to remain in Sim is strictly prohibited and may result in having trading privileges revoked.

 

What are the benefits of trading a Live account versus Sim?
If you are selected to move to trading live, you have the ability to earn an unlimited income with no withdrawal limits as a professional trader. Not only will your consistency rule be removed, you will have the ability to withdraw profits every 24 hours.

 

How long does it take to receive my live account?
Once you have been approved to move to live, your live account will be set up with the broker in 2 to 3 weeks.

 

What is the minimum withdrawal?
The minimum withdrawal amount is $200.

 

Can I withdraw from my starting balance?
No. Withdrawals are available from profits created on top of your starting balance. Example: on a live account, you will start with a $0 balance. You must have a positive balance in order to withdraw.

 

Can I purchase or continue to trade an Evaluation account or Sim Funded account if I am trading in a live account?
No, once you are trading live, you may not purchase additional accounts unless you are in the Pre-Live stage. If you are in the Pre-Live stage, you may purchase and trade on one Evaluation account. However, you will not be eligible for payouts on that Evaluation account, and you will not be able to upgrade to a SIM Funded account while in Pre-Live.

 

What will happen to my Sim Funded accounts when I am in a live account?
If you have an active account when you transition to a Live Account, that account will be closed.

 

What if I lose my live account?
Should you lose your Live Account, the risk management team will determine the appropriate next steps for the trader, based on their trading activities across all accounts associated with their profile.

 

What are the costs in the Live account?
There are no account or platform costs in live, but as a live trader, you are responsible for the professional market data. You will need to subscribe to receive Professional Data Subscription(s). Top One Futures does not make a profit on these data fees. Our trading platform charges us these fees that are passed along to you as the trader.

Prohibited Trading Practices

The full list of trading practices that are prohibited on all Top One Futures accounts, and how violations are enforced.

Updated this week

At Top One Futures, our mission is to build a sustainable, secure, and trustworthy trading environment for serious traders who value opportunity and integrity. We are deeply committed to maintaining the long-term viability of our firm and the safety of our trading ecosystem. This article lists the trading practices that are strictly forbidden on all Top One Futures accounts, regardless of account type or stage.

 

How we enforce these rules

To uphold these standards, we leverage advanced fraud detection technologies and robust compliance monitoring systems. Any trader found to be violating our rules or exploiting platform vulnerabilities will have their account breached and all associated profits forfeited. Any violations of these rules during the Elite Evaluation Phase might result in either a retake Evaluation being issued or a full breach of the account, depending on the severity of the violation.

 

1. Exploiting system, pricing, or latency errors

Any attempt to take advantage of errors, delays, mispricings, or lags in the broker's feed, the charting platform, or any associated systems will result in immediate account breach. This includes latency arbitrage and price manipulation.

 

2. Use of insider or non-public information

Trading based on information not available to the general public, including insider news or confidential financial disclosures, is prohibited.

 

3. Front-running

Placing trades with the intent to benefit from anticipated price movement based on trades executed elsewhere (for example in another account or at another firm) is not allowed.

 

4. Hedging between accounts

You may not hedge one account against another, whether within Top One Futures or across other prop firms or brokers. All trades must reflect independent trading strategies without cross-account hedging.

 

5. Unauthorized account access

Only the registered account owner is permitted to trade. Allowing friends, family, or third parties to access or trade on your account violates this policy.

 

6. Minimum trade duration (10-second rule)

To protect against ultra-high-frequency scalping and promote responsible trading:

All trades must remain open longer than 10 seconds. 10.00 seconds = violation, 10.01 seconds = acceptable.

Closing any portion of a trade before 10 seconds violates this rule.

Adding to a trade (for example scaling in) within 10 seconds is permitted.

Occasional minor violations are tolerable, but if anywhere close to 50% or more of your total and/or withdrawable profits, or anywhere close to 50% or more of your individual trades violate this rule, all profits associated with these trades will be removed.

Example

	

Result




You open a trade and add more contracts after 5 seconds. You close everything after 15 seconds.

	

Compliant




You open 2 contracts, close 1 after 5 seconds, and hold the other.

	

Violation: part of the position was closed too soon

7. Trading that risks broker relationships

Trading strategies or behaviors that may harm our broker relationships, such as abnormal flow, slippage targeting, or mass quote stuffing, are grounds for account closure.

 

8. Trading that may create regulatory concerns

Any activity that could cause regulatory exposure for Top One Futures or our liquidity partners is not tolerated.

 

9. Externally marketed evaluation-passing strategies

Using any publicly available or purchased system advertised to help traders "pass Evaluation" is not allowed. All strategies must be developed and executed by the trader.

 

10. Rolling, churning, or gambling accounts

Creating multiple evaluation accounts in a short period and using a batch-style approach, such as intentionally letting most accounts fail while focusing on passing just one, is strictly prohibited. Excessive account creation within a short timeframe, especially when done repeatedly, is considered manipulative and will be flagged by our systems.

 

We do not support gambling behavior. This includes consistently breaching accounts within 24 to 48 hours of purchase and then immediately repurchasing new accounts, indicative of toxic trading strategies. Such actions are not indicative of consistency or skill but instead reflect reckless trading strategies intended to exploit asymmetric risk at scale. Traders engaging in this type of behavior are not aligned with our long-term vision and may be permanently disqualified.

 

Example of disqualifiable churning behavior: purchasing multiple batch accounts and breaching newly purchased accounts within 1 to 2 days of trading and repeating the cycle. Day 1: trader purchased 9 accounts, all breached within 24 hours. Day 2: trader purchased 7 more accounts, again all breached within 24 hours. This shows no sustainable risk management or strategy and instead indicates a trial-and-error "gambling" style of trading, attempting to maximize short-term sim funded payout potential through unsustainable trading approaches.

 

11. Arbitrage with other firms

Attempting to gain an advantage by arbitraging trades across Top One Futures and another firm or platform is prohibited.

 

12. Automated trading / Expert Advisors (EAs)

Use of any automated trading system, script, bot, Expert Advisor (EA), or high-frequency execution tool is strictly forbidden. All trades must be entered manually or semi-manually by the trader.

 

13. Copy trading or group trading

Each trader must operate independently. The following are not allowed:

Executing the same trades as another person or account

Coordinated trading with relatives or friends

Following signal services, Telegram groups, Discord calls, or any shared trade alert system

Note on copy trading between firms: we understand that some traders now use third-party platforms to mirror their trades across multiple firms. Top One Futures allows copy trading between your own accounts at different firms. Your master account may be held at Top One Futures or another firm, provided all accounts involved are owned by you and all trades reflect your own strategy and discretion. Copying trades from accounts owned by anyone else is strictly prohibited, even with their permission. However, any behavior resembling signal following, group trading, or mirroring someone else's trades remains strictly prohibited. Top One Futures expects unique strategies per trader, not correlated or synchronized actions.

 

14. Intentional account breaching (sim farming)

Traders may not attempt to deliberately fail or breach funded accounts to avoid transitioning to live trading, remain on simulated accounts, or game system protections.

 

15. Maximum funded accounts per household

Each account type has its own maximum number of active funded accounts per household, regardless of whether the accounts belong to different individuals living at the same address. The limits per account type are:

10 in total at the same time. Elite ACCESS and Elite ACCESS Intraday count together toward one shared limit.

Important: You are allowed to purchase more accounts, e.g. to benefit from a certain promotion, but you must contact our support who will pause your excessive accounts. If you trade or activate more accounts than your limit, the oldest of your existing active accounts will be automatically breached and no refunds will be issued for that account. This rule is non-negotiable and enforced automatically by our system to maintain fairness and manage risk.
​

Please note that you can't trade different account sizes or account types together. For more details, check out our Copy Trading Policy.

 

Copy trading violations: profits made through the violation may be removed, and any related payout request could be denied. In serious or repeated cases, the accounts involved may be terminated.

 

Our philosophy: fairness for serious traders

Top One Futures is dedicated to supporting disciplined, honest, and skilled traders. We strive to offer:

Transparent rules

Rapid support

Reliable execution

Opportunities to grow and scale responsibly

Honest traders have nothing to worry about. If you trade fairly, follow the rules, and respect our community standards, we will stand behind you 100%. Those who seek to exploit the system or game the platform, however, will be swiftly detected, and consequences will apply without exception.

Questions or concerns?

Our Support Team is here to assist you with any clarifications. Please contact us through your dashboard or official communication channels for further assistance.

At Top One Futures, safeguarding the integrity of our trading platform is a top priority. To maintain a secure and fair environment for all traders, we actively monitor IP address activity across all accounts. This article explains what is allowed, what is not, and how to use a VPS correctly.

When is proof of travel required?

IP address violations

The following actions are considered violations of our security protocols:

Violation

	

Detail




Multiple IP addresses on the same account

	

Using multiple IP addresses to access a single account may raise flags and be considered a violation

Hedging across multiple accounts

Recommendations for secure trading

We highly recommend that traders use a single device with a unique IP address for their trading activities to avoid any security concerns. For professional traders, utilizing a Virtual Private Server (VPS) with a static IP address can provide additional security and faster execution times.

 

While we understand that you may trade from different devices (such as mobile or desktop) or while traveling, this may result in multiple IP addresses being associated with your account. For this reason, using a VPN may trigger location violations and lead to account suspension or breaches. We are committed to ensuring a safe and secure trading environment and use sophisticated fraud detection technology to monitor activity. The one account per user policy, prohibited registration actions, KYC identity verification, and the consequences of violations.

October 15, 2026

To maintain a fair, secure, and compliant trading environment for all of our traders, we enforce strict rules regarding account registration and ownership. Please review these policies carefully before creating your profile.

 

The single account policy

We operate under a strict one account per user policy. Every trader is permitted to have only one registered profile within our system. All of your activities, including purchasing evaluations, taking Evaluations, and managing funded accounts, must be conducted through this single, original profile.

 

Strictly prohibited actions

To ensure the integrity of our platform, several actions are strictly forbidden:

Prohibited action

	

Detail




Multiple profiles

	

You may not register for more than one user profile under any circumstances. Creating new accounts using different email addresses to bypass rules, restart an Evaluation, or mask your identity is prohibited




Registering under another identity

Third-party trading

	

You must be the sole individual executing trades on your account. Sharing your login credentials or allowing a third party to trade on your behalf is not allowed

Identity verification (KYC)

To enforce these policies, all traders must pass a Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification process before receiving any payouts. Your registered profile name must exactly match your government issued ID. If we discover that your profile details do not match your legal identity, your account will fail the verification process.

Submitting a counterfeit, forged, edited or altered document during verification is also a violation of these policies and leads to the same consequences listed below. You must also complete the verification on your own, without anyone else assisting you or being present. If we notice that you were assisted during the verification, the same consequences apply.

 

Consequences of policy violations

We actively monitor our platform for duplicate accounts and proxy trading. If our system or risk management team detects a violation of our registration rules, strict actions will be taken:

Profits forfeited

	

Any accumulated profits or pending payouts across all connected accounts will be voided and forfeited

This article will explain how the 25% consistency rule works in the Elite Sim Funded accounts

October 2, 2026

At Top One Futures, we prioritize disciplined and sustainable trading practices. One of our key risk management guidelines is the Consistency Rule, set at 25% on Elite Sim Funded accounts (20% for Instant Sim Funded Accounts) that have been upgraded from Evaluation accounts. Note: there is no consistency rule in the Elite Evaluation phase.

 

Please note: for the purposes of consistency rule calculation, a trading day ends at 5:00pm EST.

 

What is the Consistency Rule?

To become eligible for a payout, the Consistency Rule requires that no single trading day's profit accounts for more than 25% of your total profits. After a payout is taken on an Elite Sim Funded account, your total profits reset, and the consistency rule begins again based on new profits moving forward. This ensures that traders demonstrate steady performance rather than relying on one or two highly volatile trading sessions.

 

How is the 25% Consistency Rule Calculated?

The rule is based on your total profits over the entire period of having your account. No single day's profit should exceed 25% of the total profits. The consistency rule is calculated from the first day of trading until you receive a payout. After each payout, the consistency rule resets and you will need to maintain the same consistency % to qualify for the next payout.

 

For example:

If your total profit is $10,000, then no single trading day should account for more than $2,500 (25% of $10,000).

If one of your trading days results in a $3,000 profit while your total profits are $10,000, you wouldn't meet the consistency rule, and would not be eligible for a payout. Once your total profits reach $12,000, you would then meet the consistency rule (25% of $12,000 = $3,000).

How Can I Ensure Compliance with the Consistency Rule?

Plan your trades carefully to avoid making excessive profits in a single day.

Spread your gains evenly over multiple trading days.

Avoid trading with high risk or taking highly volatile trades that can lead to outsized profits.

Monitor your progress regularly to ensure no single trading day surpasses the 25% threshold.

This article explains about the Max Loss Limit (MLL) on the Elite Daily V2 Accounts

Updated over 3 weeks ago

The Max Loss Limit (MLL) is the maximum total loss your account can sustain before it is permanently breached. Unlike the Daily Loss Limit, the MLL is based on an End of Day (EOD) trailing drawdown model.

 

Good to know: the MLL level moves up only at the end of the trading day, based on your closing balance, and locks in at your starting balance + $100 once your account has grown enough. The breach level is checked in real time. If your equity goes at or below it at any moment, the account is breached. There are no warnings when the MLL is breached.

How the End of Day Trailing Drawdown Works

The MLL follows a trailing model, but it only adjusts at the end of each trading day. This means:

Your breach level is active from the moment you start: starting balance minus your max drawdown (e.g. $50,000 − $2,000 = $48,000).

It trails upward as your account reaches new highs.

It moves up only at the end of the day, based on your closing balance. Intraday highs don’t move it.

It does not move down if your balance decreases.

The breach level is checked in real time. If your equity goes at or below it at any moment, the account is breached.

 

As your account grows, the drawdown level locks in at your starting balance + $100 and does not continue to trail.

Opening a trade

October 1, 2026

Funded Elite ACCESS accounts do not have a profit target to keep the account active, but they do have a minimum profit requirement before you can request a payout. To become payout eligible, your account must reach the required profit level above the payout buffer.

How it works

Before requesting a payout, your account must first build the required buffer, plus an additional $500 in profit. This means:

The buffer must remain in the account.

How the Daily Loss Limit works on Elite ACCESS: none during the evaluation, a soft breach on the funded account.

Updated this week

The Daily Loss Limit (DLL) is the maximum amount your account can lose within a single trading day. On Elite ACCESS it applies only to the funded account. There is no Daily Loss Limit during the evaluation.

 

Evaluation phase

There is no Daily Loss Limit during the evaluation phase.

You are not restricted by a daily loss limit.

Your only risk limit is the EOD trailing drawdown.

You can trade freely within the overall drawdown rules.

Funded phase (soft breach)

Updated over 3 weeks ago

The Maximum Loss Limit (MLL), also known as the EOD trailing drawdown, is the maximum amount your account can lose overall. It applies during both the evaluation and the funded phase and trails on an end-of-day (EOD) basis.

How the trailing works

Your breach level is active from the moment you start: starting balance minus your max drawdown (e.g. $50,000 − $2,000 = $48,000).

It trails upward as your account reaches new highs.

It moves up only at the end of the day, based on your closing balance. Intraday highs don’t move it.

It does not move down if your balance decreases.

The breach level is checked in real time. If your equity goes at or below it at any moment, the account is breached.

Elite ACCESS – Funded Consistency Rule (40%)

The 40% consistency rule on funded Elite ACCESS accounts: how it is calculated and when it is checked.

October 1, 2026

The Consistency Rule ensures that trading performance is stable and not reliant on a single large trading day. It applies only to funded accounts.

 

How the 40% rule works

Your largest single trading day must not exceed 40% of your total profits in your current payout cycle.

 

Formula: Consistency % = (Largest winning day ÷ Total profit) × 100. This value must be 40% or less.

Example

	

Total profit

When the rule applies

The consistency rule is checked when you submit a payout request, based on your current total profit at that moment.

 

How to get below the 40% mark

If your account exceeds the 40% limit, continue trading to increase your total profit, which reduces the percentage impact of your largest winning day.

 

Example: your largest day is $2,000. To be compliant (40% or less), your total profit must be at least $5,000.

 

Good to know

Applies only to funded accounts.

Applies only to profitable days.

Based on closed trades only.

Recalculated continuously as your profit changes.

After a payout is taken, your total profits reset and the consistency rule starts again based on new profits moving forward.

Your largest winning day may never be more than 40% of the total profit in your current payout cycle. If it is, keep trading until it is.

Everything you need before you can request a payout on a funded Elite ACCESS account, in one place.

October 1, 2026

Elite ACCESS funded accounts offer on-demand payouts, as long as all payout conditions are met. To request a payout you must satisfy all requirements below: the 40% consistency rule, the buffer and profit requirement, the minimum profitable days and the daily progression rule.

Payout buffer and profit requirement

Before requesting a payout, your account must reach the required profit level: the buffer plus $500.

The buffer must remain in the account at all times.

You can only withdraw profits above the required profit level.

Each payout request must meet this threshold.

Minimum profitable days

You need a minimum of 5 profitable trading days before each payout. A day only counts when it reaches the minimum daily profit for your account size (see the table above).

 

Consistency rule (40%)

Your largest winning day must not exceed 40% of your total profits in your current payout cycle. If this rule is not yet met, the payout cannot be requested yet and you may continue trading until compliant.

 

After a payout is taken, your total profits reset and the consistency rule starts again based on new profits moving forward. This ensures that traders demonstrate steady performance.

 

50% profit progression rule

For each payout request, at least 50% of the requested payout amount must come from profits generated since your last payout. There is no restriction on your first payout; from the second payout onward, at least 50% must come from new profits.

 

Profit split

90% of the payout goes to the trader and 10% to the firm.

 

Path to Live

Your payouts also count toward moving from a simulated funded account to a live funded account.

3 successful payouts are required before you become eligible for the transition.

Once you reach this milestone, a risk manager reviews your trading performance.

If approved, your account is transitioned to live, where you trade with real capital.

Only one account transitions to live. If you hold multiple accounts, one account moves over and your remaining accounts are closed at that point. For full details, see the Path to Trading Live article.

Checklist before you request a payout: 5 profitable days, balance above buffer + $500, largest day at most 40% of total profit, at least 50% new profit since your last payout, and a request of at least $500.

Elite ACCESS – News Trading Rule
Elite ACCESS – News Trading Rule

The 2-minute news trading restriction on funded Elite ACCESS accounts: what is restricted, which events count and what happens on a violation.

October 1, 2026

Trading around major economic news events carries increased risk due to volatility, slippage and rapid price movements. On Elite ACCESS, news trading restrictions apply only to funded accounts.

 

Where the rule applies

Stage

	

News restriction




Evaluation

	

No restrictions. News trading is fully allowed.




Funded

	

2-minute restricted window before and after high-impact news.

Funded news restriction window

On funded accounts you may not execute trades 2 minutes before and 2 minutes after a high-impact news event. The total restricted window is 4 minutes.

 

The following actions are not allowed during the restricted window:

Opening a trade

Closing a trade

Opening pending orders

Placing stop or limit orders

Modifying a stop loss

Modifying a take profit

Any of the above during the restricted window is considered a rule violation.

 

Holding trades during news

You may hold positions during news only if the trade was opened before the 2-minute pre-news window. However:

If a trade is closed during the restricted window, it is a violation.

If the SL or TP is modified during the window, it is a violation.

If a trade is closed by any means (manual or automatic) during the window, it is a violation.

What happens if the rule is violated

Profits from the violating trade may be removed.

The payout request may be denied.

The account may be flagged for review.

Repeated or abusive violations may lead to further action. Violations do not automatically result in a hard breach unless abuse is detected.

 

Which news events are restricted

Only high-impact economic events are restricted. This includes, but is not limited to:

FOMC announcements

Interest rate decisions

Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP)

CPI releases

Major central bank statements

If an event is marked as high impact (red) on the official economic calendar used by Top One Futures, it falls under this rule. Low and medium impact events are not restricted. You can monitor high-impact events with the FXStreet Economic Calendar.

Disclaimer: trading during news events carries inherent risks, including slippage, delayed execution and market gaps. Top One Futures is not responsible for losses caused by market volatility. Traders are responsible for managing their own risk at all times.

October 1, 2026

Even professional traders face volatile days. That is why Elite ACCESS accounts have a reset option for both the evaluation and the funded account, so you can restart your journey if your account is breached.

 

Reset fees

The evaluation reset has a fixed fee of $35 for every account size. The funded reset restores your account to its starting balance without having to pass the evaluation again, and depends on your account size.

How a reset works

Fresh start: your account is restored to its original starting balance.

Clean slate: your previous profit and loss history is cleared.

Eligibility: a reset is only available within 14 days from the date the account was breached.

Fixed pricing: discounts and coupons are not applicable to reset fees.

Same conditions: a reset account is recreated with the same profit target and drawdown parameters as your original account.

When to use a reset

If you exceed the maximum daily drawdown or total drawdown and breach your account.

If your balance falls below the allowed limit and you want another chance to trade your strategy.

If you want a fresh start without the time commitment of starting a new evaluation.

A reset must be bought within 14 days of the breach. After that, the account can no longer be reset.

Key takeaway: the TIDD follows your highest equity value ever achieved, whether realized or unrealized. It does not reset when you close a trade.

 

When does the TIDD stop trailing (drawdown lock)

On funded Elite ACCESS Intraday accounts, the TIDD keeps trailing until you request your first payout. After your first payout request, it locks at starting balance + $100 and stops trailing. From that point, account growth no longer raises the breach level. This is different from the evaluation phase and from the regular Elite ACCESS account, where the drawdown locks as soon as the balance reaches starting balance + drawdown + $100. On a funded Elite ACCESS Intraday account the drawdown keeps trailing above that level until your first payout request.

 

Good to know

Real-time: includes open (unrealized) trades.

Dynamic: adjusts upward as new equity highs are hit, never down.

Breach level: if your equity drops below the trailing threshold, your account breaches.

Post-payout lock: after your first payout, the TIDD locks at starting balance + $100.

This rule rewards discipline, not gambling. Traders who manage risk and grow steadily will thrive.

Hard breach: if your equity drops at or below the Maximum Loss Limit threshold during the funded phase, the account is permanently breached and trading access is disabled.

October 1, 2026

The Consistency Rule ensures that trading performance is stable and not reliant on a single large trading day. It applies only to funded accounts; there is no consistency rule during the evaluation.

 

How the 40% rule works

Your largest single trading day must not exceed 40% of your total profits in your current payout cycle.

 

Formula: Consistency % = (Largest winning day ÷ Total profit) × 100. This value must be 40% or less. To find the minimum total profit you need based on your best day: Total profit needed = Largest winning day ÷ 0.40.

If your account exceeds the 40% limit, continue trading to increase your total profit, which reduces the percentage impact of your largest winning day.

 

Example: your largest day is $2,000. To be compliant (40% or less), your total profit must be at least $5,000.

Payout buffer and profit requirement

Before requesting a payout, your account must reach the required profit level: the buffer plus $500.

The buffer must remain in the account at all times.

You can only withdraw profits above the required profit level.

Each payout request must meet this threshold.

Minimum profitable days

You need a minimum of 5 profitable trading days before each payout. A day only counts when it reaches the minimum daily profit for your account size (see the table above).

 

Consistency rule (40%)

Your largest winning day must not exceed 40% of your total profits in your current payout cycle. If this rule is not yet met, the payout cannot be requested yet and you may continue trading until compliant.

 

After a payout is taken, your total profits reset and the consistency rule starts again based on new profits moving forward. This ensures that traders demonstrate steady performance.

 

50% profit progression rule

For each payout request, at least 50% of the requested payout amount must come from profits generated since your last payout. There is no restriction on your first payout; from the second payout onward, at least 50% must come from new profits generated after your previous payout request.

 

Profit split

90% of the payout goes to the trader and 10% to the firm.

 

Path to Live

Your payouts also count toward moving from a simulated funded account to a live funded account.

3 successful payouts are required before you become eligible for the transition.

Once you reach this milestone, a risk manager reviews your trading performance.

If approved, your account is transitioned to live, where you trade with real capital.

Only one account transitions to live. If you hold multiple accounts, one account moves over and your remaining accounts are closed at that point. For full details, see the Path to Trading Live article.

Checklist before you request a payout: 5 profitable days, balance above buffer + $500, largest day at most 40% of total profit, at least 50% new profit since your last payout, and a request of at least $500.

Elite ACCESS Intraday - News Trading Rule

The 2-minute news trading restriction on funded Elite ACCESS Intraday accounts: what is restricted, which events count and what happens on a violation.

October 1, 2026

Trading around major economic news events carries increased risk due to volatility, slippage and rapid price movements. On Elite ACCESS Intraday, news trading restrictions apply only to funded accounts.

 

Where the rule applies

Stage

	

News restriction




Evaluation

	

No restrictions. News trading is fully allowed.




Funded

	

2-minute restricted window before and after high-impact news.

Funded news restriction window

On funded accounts you may not execute trades 2 minutes before and 2 minutes after a high-impact news event. The total restricted window is 4 minutes.

 

The following actions are not allowed during the restricted window:

Opening a trade

Closing a trade

Opening pending orders

Placing stop or limit orders

Modifying a stop loss

Modifying a take profit

Any of the above during the restricted window is considered a rule violation.

 

Holding trades during news

You may hold positions during news only if the trade was opened before the 2-minute pre-news window. However:

If a trade is closed during the restricted window, it is a violation.

If the SL or TP is modified during the window, it is a violation.

If a trade is closed by any means (manual or automatic) during the window, it is a violation.

What happens if the rule is violated

Profits from the violating trade may be removed.

The payout request may be denied.

The account may be flagged for review.

Repeated or abusive violations may lead to further action. Violations do not automatically result in a hard breach unless abuse is detected.

 

Which news events are restricted

Only high-impact economic events are restricted. This includes, but is not limited to:

FOMC announcements

Interest rate decisions

Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP)

CPI releases

Major central bank statements

If an event is marked as high impact (red) on the official economic calendar used by Top One Futures, it falls under this rule. Low and medium impact events are not restricted.

Funded accounts only: no opening, closing or modifying of trades from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after a red (high-impact) news event.

Consistency Rule in Instant Sim Funded Accounts Explained

How the 20% Consistency Rule works on Instant Sim Funded accounts, how it is calculated, and tips to stay within it.

October 1, 2026

At Top One Futures, we prioritize disciplined and sustainable trading. One of our key risk management guidelines on Instant Sim Funded accounts is the Consistency Rule, set at 20%. This article explains what the rule is, how it is calculated, and how you can stay within it.

 

What is the Consistency Rule?

The Consistency Rule requires that no single trading day accounts for more than 20% of your total profits at the time of a payout request. Your consistency score is calculated as your highest profit day divided by your total profits, and it must be 20% or lower before a payout can be approved.

Rule detail

	

How it works




Threshold

	

Highest profit day may be at most 20% of total profits




When it is checked

	

At the time of each payout request




After a payout

	

The consistency calculation resets and starts fresh




Trading day

	

Ends at 5:00 PM EST

How is the Consistency Rule calculated?

Divide your highest profit day by your total profits. If your total profits are $10,000, your highest single trading day may not exceed $2,000 (20%). A day of $3,000 on the same total would be 30%, so the account would not yet be eligible for a payout. You would need to continue trading until total profits reach at least $15,000, bringing that day back to 20%.

The highest day is $2,300, which is 23% of $10,000, so the trader does not pass yet. After adding another $1,500 in profit (total $11,500), the $2,300 day drops to 20% and the account becomes eligible for a payout.

 

Tips to stay within the rule

Plan your trades: avoid chasing oversized gains on a single day.

Spread your gains: consistent, moderate profits across multiple days keep your score low.

Avoid high risk exposure: large positions can produce one outsized day that blocks your payout.

Monitor your score: track your highest day against your total profits before requesting a payout.

Please note: the Consistency Rule does not fail or close your account. If your highest day exceeds 20% of total profits, simply keep trading with consistent results until the ratio is back at 20% or lower, then request your payout.

How the 15% consistency rule on Ignite accounts is calculated, with pass and fail examples and how to fix a high score.

October 1, 2026

The 15% Consistency Rule ensures that funded Ignite traders earn profits through a stable, consistent strategy rather than from a single lucky or high-risk trading day. We partner with traders who can demonstrate steady, long-term profitability, and this rule rewards that skill.

 

This rule applies to new Ignite accounts opened under the updated terms. Existing accounts that use the ESS rule remain unchanged and cannot transition to this rule.

 

The rule and how it is calculated

Your single best trading day’s profit cannot account for more than 15% of your total accumulated profit. At the moment you request a payout, we check your score with this formula:

 

Consistency score = (Best day’s profit ÷ Total profit) × 100. To be eligible for a payout, your score must be 15% or lower.

Failed? How to fix a high score

You do not need to panic or reset your account. The solution is to continue trading profitably to increase your total profit. Your one big day has set a new, higher profit target for you:

 

New target profit = Best day’s profit ÷ 0.15. Using scenario 2: $2,000 ÷ 0.15 = $13,333.33. You must grow your total profit to $13,333.33 to bring your score down to 15% (assuming you do not have another, even larger winning day on the way).

 

Good to know

It is a payout rule. This rule does not cause a breach. It is only checked when you request a withdrawal.

It encourages longevity. The best way to pass is to aim for smaller, consistent daily wins rather than hitting your entire target in one or two days.

It resets. The consistency score calculation resets to zero after every successful payout.

Your best day may never be more than 15% of your total profit at the moment you request a payout. If it is, keep trading until the total catches up: new target = best day ÷ 0.15.

How the trailing works

Your breach level is active from the moment you start: starting balance minus your max drawdown (e.g. $50,000 − $3,000 = $47,000 on a $50,000 funded account).

It trails upward as your account reaches new highs.

The breach level is checked in real time. If your equity goes at or below it at any moment, the account is breached.

Hard breach: if your account equity goes at or below the breach level at any time, the account fails.

How scaling works

Once your account is funded, your maximum contract size increases as your account grows. Your allowed contract size is determined by your end-of-day (EOD) closing balance and updates once per trading day.

 

Key principles

Scaling applies only to funded accounts. There are no scaling rules during the evaluation.

Contract limits update once per day (EOD).

Scaling is based on simulated profit.

You must stay within your allowed contract size at all times.

How scaling is calculated

Your level is determined by your funded account's end-of-day closing balance, in other words your total simulated profit (closing balance minus starting balance).

 

Contract increases are applied the following trading day once your closing balance qualifies.

Intraday profits do not unlock a higher level.

Only end-of-day results are used.

Your level can also go down

Scaling works in both directions. If your end-of-day balance drops below the threshold for your current level, your contract limit is reduced to the matching lower level from the following trading day. This also applies after a payout: a payout lowers your balance, so your level is recalculated from the new balance.

 

Example ($50,000 account): You close a day at $52,100, which puts you on Level 3 (4 minis). The next day you close at $51,500. From the following trading day your limit is Level 2 (3 minis) again.

 

Trader responsibility

It is your responsibility to monitor and follow the contract scaling rules at all times. Exceeding your allowed contract size is a rule violation. If scaling rules are not followed:

Trades may be rejected or reduced

The account may be flagged for review

Profits from violating trades may be removed

Payout requests may be denied

Compliance with scaling rules is required for payout eligibility.

 

Important clarifications

Scaling applies per individual account. Contract limits do not combine across accounts.

Scaling is based on simulated profit only.

Limits are determined using the end-of-day balance.

Scaling does not override other risk rules such as the Daily Loss Limit (DLL) and the Maximum Loss Limit (MLL).

Balance After Payout #2: $157,000 ($166,000 – $9,000). This $157,000 becomes your new baseline for Payout #3.

Scenario B (Denied / Limited): You request $9,000, but only made $4,000 in new profit

Suppose your balance grew from $155,000 to $159,000 ($4,000 in new profit; $9,000 total profit above initial starting capital).

You attempt to request a $9,000 payout:

50% Rule Requirement: 50% of $9,000 = $4,500 in new profit required.

Your New Profit: $4,000.

Status: DENIED. You are $500 short of the required $4,500 in new profit.

How the end of day trailing max drawdown works on X-Daily Spark

Updated over 3 weeks ago

The max drawdown (MLL) is the most your account can lose before it is permanently breached. On X-Daily Spark it is $2,000, trailing on an end of day (EOD) basis, on both the evaluation and the funded account.

 

Max drawdown by stage

How EOD trailing works

Your breach level is active from the moment you start: starting balance minus your max drawdown (e.g. $50,000 − $2,000 = $48,000).

It trails upward as your account reaches new highs.

It moves up only at the end of the day, based on your closing balance. Intraday highs don’t move it.

It does not move down if your balance decreases.

The breach level is checked in real time. If your equity goes at or below it at any moment, the account is breached.

Static evaluation drawdown add-on

For +$15 at checkout, your evaluation drawdown becomes static. Your breach level stays at $48,000 for the whole evaluation and does not trail.

 

What happens if you hit it

If your account equity goes at or below the breach level at any time, it is permanently breached. Funded accounts cannot be reset. To trade X-Daily Spark again, buy a new evaluation ($39) and pay the activation fee ($189) when you pass.

Please note: there are no warnings when the max drawdown is hit.

How a payout locks your maximum trailing drawdown at the starting balance plus $100, with an example and tips to keep a buffer.

October 2, 2026

When you request a payout, your maximum trailing drawdown locks in at the starting balance plus $100. From the moment you make a payout, the drawdown no longer trails with your account growth, regardless of how much you continue to grow your account.

 

How the lock upon payout works

When you qualify for and request a payout, the maximum drawdown locks in at your initial account balance plus $100. Here is an example to illustrate this:

Example

	

Value




Initial balance

	

$100,000




Balance after profit

	

$105,000




Payout request

	

$3,000




New balance after payout

	

$102,000




Locked drawdown

	

$100,100

In this case, after your $3,000 payout, your maximum drawdown locks in at $100,100, leaving you with $1,900 of drawdown room before reaching your limit.

 

Important considerations

It is wise to leave a decent buffer so you do not breach your account. To avoid this, we have a couple of recommendations for you:

Recommendation

	

Why




Leave some sim profits as a buffer

	

Instead of withdrawing the maximum amount of your sim profits, consider leaving some in your account. This will give you more breathing room and reduce the risk of breaching your account




Grow your account further

	

Another option is to grow your account by an additional 5% or more before taking your payout. This will give you a larger cushion and increase the likelihood of growing and compounding your account

Of course, the decision is ultimately yours. We are happy to process your payout, but our goal is to see you have many successful payouts with us in the future. We do not want you to jeopardize your account in any way.

 

Why this rule exists

The drawdown lock upon payout is designed to ensure long-term sustainability for both traders and the firm. This rule encourages traders to focus on long-term growth and compounding, which can lead to significantly larger payouts over time. By locking the drawdown at the starting balance after a withdrawal, traders are incentivized to manage their accounts with discipline and focus on continued growth.

NinjaTrader performs routine maintenance throughout the week. During these maintenance windows, new accounts cannot be created and will remain in a pending queue until maintenance is completed. If you purchase a Tradovate / NinjaTrader account during these hours, it may not appear immediately. This is normal and expected.

 

No action needed: your account is created automatically once NinjaTrader's maintenance has finished, usually within 15 minutes. Support cannot manually speed up the creation during maintenance.

 

NinjaTrader Maintenance Schedule (Central Time)

Below is the official NinjaTrader maintenance schedule.

 

Type

	

Days

	

Time (CT)




Weekday Maintenance

	

Monday to Thursday

	

4:00 PM to 5:00 PM CT




Friday Maintenance

What This Means for Your Purchase

Using ATM Strategies in NinjaTrader Desktop

Important information for traders using ATM strategies on Tradovate/Ninjatrader accounts

October 2, 2026

ATM (Advanced Trade Management) Strategies in NinjaTrader Desktop allow you to automatically place Stop Loss and Take Profit orders and add optional automation such as breakeven and trailing stops. They help make trade management faster and more consistent. Below is everything you need to know when using ATM Strategies with a Tradovate-backed Top One Futures trading account.

 

Most important: ATM Strategies are 100% client-side. They run only on your local NinjaTrader Desktop, not on the server and not on Tradovate. If NinjaTrader Desktop is not open, running and connected, no ATM instructions can be sent.

 

What Are ATM Strategies? (Quick Overview)

ATM Strategies allow you to predefine:

Take Profit

Stop Loss

Trade quantity

Auto Breakeven

Auto Trail (trailing stop)

OCO behavior

Multi-target layouts

Saved ATM templates

 

They are completely optional. You can trade manually or use ATMs for convenience and consistency.

 

ATM Strategies Are 100% Client-Side

This is the most important thing to understand. ATM Strategies do not run on the server and do not run on Tradovate. They run only on your local NinjaTrader Desktop. Because of this, ATM features work only when NinjaTrader Desktop is open, running, and connected. If your NinjaTrader Desktop isn't running, the ATM cannot calculate or send any instructions to the server.

 

Example 1: Trade Is Active, ATM placed TP/SL, You disconnect

You enter a trade and your ATM strategy immediately places a Stop Loss and Take Profit. Those orders are now on the server, so they stay active. But if you use any of the features below, they will be impacted when you are disconnected in any way:

The trailing stop will stop trailing

The breakeven trigger will not activate

No further ATM updates will happen

Many other features will not update

 

Your original TP and SL that were placed will stay, as they have been received by the server, but all automation stops.

 

Example 2: You Place a Limit Order, You Disconnect, The Order Fills

This scenario is very important, because many traders assume ATM Strategies will still trigger even if they disconnect. They will not. Here is exactly what happens:

You place a limit order with an ATM Strategy selected (placed limit orders are server-side, so they are received on Tradovate's server)

NinjaTrader Desktop disconnects (computer off, platform closed, sleep mode, internet drop, etc.)

Price reaches your limit order and the order fills on the server

But your ATM Strategy never activates, because NinjaTrader Desktop wasn't connected at the moment of the fill

 

This means:

No Stop Loss is submitted

No Take Profit is submitted

No OCO is created

No trailing or breakeven can run

Your trade is unprotected

 

The platform must be online at the moment the order fills in order for ATM instructions to be sent.

 

Keeping ATM Strategies Working Correctly

To keep ATM Strategies working correctly, your computer must remain:

Requirement

	

Status needed




Computer

	

Turned on, not in sleep / hibernation mode




Internet

	

Connected, not disconnected




NinjaTrader Desktop

	

Running and connected

 

Top One Futures Disclaimer

Top One Futures is not responsible for ATM Strategies failing due to:

Internet disconnection

Closing NinjaTrader Desktop

Device shutdown

Platform crashes

Sleep/hibernation mode

Power outages

Any local device issues

 

ATM logic is fully client-side and depends entirely on the trader's system and connection.

 

Recommended Safety Tip

Always verify that your Stop Loss and Take Profit are active on the Tradovate Web Platform: https://trader.tradovate.com

 

If TP/SL orders do not appear there, they are not active, and your ATM Strategy did not send them to the server. Any other features that update these orders (trailing stop, auto-breakeven, etc.) will not work when disconnected from NinjaTrader Desktop, even when the TP/SL orders are correctly placed on the server side.

 

Learn More About ATM Strategies

For a full breakdown of every ATM feature, please see NinjaTrader's official documentation. This explains all ATM tools in detail, including Auto Breakeven, Auto Trail, Shadow Strategy, and more.

How to copy trade on BlackArrow
October 10, 2026

BlackArrow allows you to copy trade using its built-in Order Replicator, enabling you to mirror trades across up to 10 accounts simultaneously.

 

To start configuring your Order Replicator:

Navigate to the Trade menu.

Select Replicator.

Note: If you do not see the Replicator option in your menu, please contact our support team at support@toponefutures.com so we can grant you access.

 

 

To start, click on Create Replicator.

 

 

In Master Account choose the account from which you will manually send orders. It can be your real brokerage account or your demo account.

 

Note: Automations and execution strategies cannot be used as the master account.

 

 

To complete the setup of the Master Account, click Finish" This will create the Replicator wallet. The account you selected will be linked to the module and will appear in other licenses.

 

The next step is to link the Follower Accounts to the Replicator, meaning the accounts that will automatically replicate the orders sent from the Master Account selected in the previous step.

To do this, you will need to follow the steps below for each of the follower account licenses. In other words, after completing the steps for one account, you should switch between licenses to configure the others.

Once you have accessed the follower license, go to the Trade menu, select Replicator and click on Follow to link the account that will copy the trades.

 

 

After clicking on Follow, a window will open in which you can select the desired Follower Account.

 

To complete the setup, click Finish. 

 

Note: It is possible to adjust the settings so that the orders are replicated identically or up to 10 times the amount performed on the Master Account.

 

Example: When sending an order for 2 contracts on the Master Account, with the multiplier set to 2x on the Follower Account, the replicated order will be for 4 contracts.

 

To send orders, it is necessary to select the Replicator account in the trading tool.

 

 

The account will be highlighted in yellow, as shown in the example above.

All orders placed in this account will be automatically and simultaneously replicated in all accounts selected as followers, and at the multiplication factor configured by the user.

 

Important Notice Regarding BlackArrow Replicator Usage

 

While the BlackArrow replicator tool is available to assist with managing multiple accounts, traders are strongly advised to actively monitor all replicator actions, order entries, and position states in real time.

 

Top One Futures assumes no responsibility or liability for any execution errors, system delays, failed trades, unintended position reversals, or financial losses resulting from the use, configuration, or technical malfunction of the BlackArrow replicator tool. Traders utilize replication features entirely at their own risk and remain solely responsible for supervising their accounts and managing active market exposure at all times.

How to Copy Trade on WealthCharts
How to Copy Trade on WealthCharts
October 9, 2026
Overview & Navigation

To locate the Trade Copier, select the Main Menu icon in the top-left corner of the platform, navigate to Trading, and select Trade Copier. You can also find it directly using the menu search bar.

 

 

 

Key Features & Setup Guide
1. Copier Strategies

The Trade Copier allows you to create and manage multiple strategies within a single component. Each configured strategy can be customized with:

A unique futures instrument/symbol

A dedicated Leader Account

A designated group of Follower Accounts

Individual Ratio and Cross settings

Rule: Duplicate symbols and leader account combinations are not permitted across strategies. If a specific leader account and symbol pair is active in one strategy, it cannot be reused in another.

 

When creating a new strategy, select the desired symbol and click the Set Strategy button to save and activate it across browser tabs.

 

 

2. Account Checkboxes

To start copying trades, check the box next to each target follower account:

Selected accounts will receive all copied trades from the designated Leader Account.

Follower accounts must be different from the Leader Account.

Click Set Strategy whenever active to save your account selections.

3. Ratio Settings

The Ratio setting acts as a contract multiplier for orders entered via the DOM or Order Panel:

Adjust the multiplier using the + / - buttons or type the value directly into the field.

Click Set Strategy to apply ratio changes.

4. Cross-Market Copying (Cross)

When Cross is enabled, trades execute in the opposing market contract type (e.g., Mini to Micro):

Example: A trade placed on ESH6 (E-mini) will automatically execute as MESH6 (Micro E-mini) on follower accounts where Cross is enabled.

Use the active symbol buttons in this column to toggle between primary and opposing market symbols.

5. Instrument / Symbol Search

Enter the symbol you wish to trade.

A valid instrument is required before trades can be copied.

Non-tradable or invalid symbols will trigger an error message. Ensure your selected symbol is supported by your Prop Firm.

6. Strategy Toggles & Sync Settings
Strategy Enable/Disable

Enabled: Trades are actively copied for the strategy.

Disabled: Pauses copying for that specific strategy without deleting your configuration.

Sync Settings

Configure how follower accounts mirror the leader account in the Sync Settings menu (by Time or Ticks):

Time Sync: Follower accounts must fill within a set time window (defined in the Sync Interval field, default is 3 seconds).

Desync Protection: If a follower fails to fill within the allotted window or fills outside the acceptable price/bracket range, it is flagged as Desynced and automatically flattened out of the copied position.

IMPORTANT: Desyncing occurs when a follower account loses alignment with the leader (e.g., bracket mismatch, setup variance, or execution delay beyond the sync threshold).

 

7. Template Manager

Save valid Trade Copier configurations as Templates to quickly switch between different setups or instruments.

Applied templates display text reading [Template Name] Applied above the button.

Manage, rename, edit, or delete saved templates directly inside the Template Manager.

 

8. Symbol Linking Behavior

When the Trade Copier is linked to an active chart:

Changing the chart symbol will not alter the Trade Copier symbol.

Changing the Trade Copier symbol (or switching strategies) will automatically update the linked chart.

This logic prevents accidental modification of active copying strategies during chart analysis.

 

9. Flattening Positions

Strategy Flatten: Click Flatten All within a specific strategy component to exit all positions for that instrument.

Individual Account Flatten: Click Flatten next to a specific account row to close only that account's position.

Leader Account Flatten: Flattening the Leader Account automatically flattens all connected Follower Accounts.

Global Emergency Flatten: The Flatten All button at the bottom of the Trade Copier component flattens open positions and cancels all working orders across all Leader and Follower accounts simultaneously.

10. Set Strategy (Critical Final Step)

The Set Strategy button confirms and commits strategy-level changes:

Must be clicked when creating new strategies, updating account selections, or altering ratios/symbols.

When action is required, the Set Strategy button highlights in blue.

Changes will not persist or synchronize across sessions/tabs until Set Strategy is pressed.

Additional Controls

Disable Copy Trading Button: Located at the bottom of the component; instantly turns off all trade copying for the current session.

Hyperprop Platform Overview
Hyperprop Platform Overview
Updated today

Hyperprop is a trading platform built for prop firm traders. Your rules, your drawdown and how much room you have left sit right next to the order panel.

 

Accounts available on Hyperprop

Elite Daily

Elite ACCESS, Elite ACCESS Intraday and Elite ACCESS Static

Ignite

Instant Sim Funded

Launchpad X-HYPER

Not available on Hyperprop: Elite Sim Funded, X-Ultra and X-Daily Spark.

You select Hyperprop at checkout, the same way you select any of our other platforms.

 

What you get

Your accounts and rules

Every account you hold on one screen, each with its own status, balance and limits

Trailing drawdown, evaluation progress, profit target and remaining drawdown shown while you trade, updating with live CME data

Copy trading included. Link a lead account to followers, and each account still keeps its own risk limits

 

Charts

Indicators, multi chart layouts, drawing tools and price alerts

Market replay, bar by bar, for practice

Write your own indicators with Hyperprop Scripts

 

Placing orders

Order panel with separate buy and sell buttons and a size stepper

Mouse click trading straight from the chart

DOM price ladder with one click entry

Brackets that link your take profit and stop loss, plus OCO linking

Keyboard shortcuts

 

Your record

An automatic journal built from your real fills, with a P&L calendar

A track record backed by fill data instead of screenshots, private unless you share it

Hyperprop runs in your browser. There is nothing to install.

 

Markets and data

CME Group futures across CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX, licensed as a single bundle. Complete the market data setup inside the platform to unlock it.

 

What is not available yet

Browser only. No desktop application and no mobile app

Top of book pricing. Full order book depth is not live, so the ladder shows prices without resting size behind them

Market, limit and stop orders only. No stop limit, market if touched, iceberg or trailing stop orders

No time in force settings. An order stays active until it fills or you cancel it

Note: A trailing stop order is not the same thing as your trailing drawdown. Your trailing drawdown is a rule on your account and it works normally on Hyperprop.

 

Your account is still with us

Hyperprop provides the platform. It does not sell accounts, take payments or move money. Your evaluation, funded account, resets and payouts are handled by Top One Futures, under the same rules that apply on any other platform.

 

Learn the platform

Help center: https://www.hyperprop.com/help/

Tutorial videos: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLTwV_EXPUY0g

 

Before you buy

Your platform choice is permanent for that account. You cannot move an account to another platform, and neither passing your evaluation nor resetting it changes that. See Can I Switch My Trading Platform?

How to Connect Your Account to Hyperprop
How to Connect Your Account to Hyperprop
Updated today

Your account links automatically when you sign in to Hyperprop with the same email you used for your purchase. If your Hyperprop login uses a different email, you link it with your import key instead.

 

Funded accounts: your funded account is created after you sign your trader agreement in your Top One Futures dashboard. Only then do you receive the Account Ready email with your import key. If your funded account doesn't appear in Hyperprop automatically, import it with that key (see the import steps below).

 

If this is your first Hyperprop account

Go to app.hyperprop.com/sign-up.

Sign up with the email you used to buy your account, and confirm it.

Your account appears under Trading Accounts automatically.

 

If you already have a Hyperprop account

Buy your account using the same email as your Hyperprop login. Then just sign in at app.hyperprop.com/sign-in and it appears under Trading Accounts automatically. Nothing else to do.

 

If you bought with a different email, or your funded account doesn't appear, use your import key:

Find the email "[Account Ready] Link your HyperProp account". It shows your account number, for example HP42001, and your import key.

Sign in at app.hyperprop.com/sign-in. Click your profile picture (top right), then Trading accounts. You can also use Trading Accounts in the left menu.

Click Add account (top right), choose Prop firm and paste your import key.

Click Import account.

How to Turn On Market Data on Hyperprop
How to Turn On Market Data on Hyperprop
Updated today

Before you can see live prices and place orders, Hyperprop asks you to finish a short setup. Until it is done, a checklist covers the chart.

 

Complete these four steps

Accept the CME market data agreement. You can check whether it is accepted under Settings.

Complete your profile. Fill in every field. A missing field is the most common reason the checklist stays open.

Link your Discord account. The link has to be fully authorized, not just started.

Have an active trading account. Your Top One Futures account counts once it is linked. An account you have not linked yet does not. See How to Connect Your Account to Hyperprop.

 

What happens next

The checklist rechecks itself every few seconds, so there is no need to refresh the page

Once every step is done, the checklist disappears and live prices load

The first time, you also get a confirmation email

 

Good to know

The data covers CME Group futures across CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX as one bundle

You only do this once, not once per account

Without market data, your orders are rejected. See Hyperprop Troubleshooting and FAQ

 

Checklist still showing?

Go through the four steps again, starting with your profile. If everything is done and the checklist is still there, contact our support team with your account number and a screenshot of the checklist.
